answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every new identity to lock a refundable stake bond before it may transact. Think of each bond as a marble dropped into escrow: one honest identity makes a small ripple, but forging ten thousand fakes drains capital terrace by terrace. Legitimate agents reclaim their bond; identities caught colluding forfeit it. Since cost rises linearly with identity count while influence per bond stays capped, an attacker always pays more than the control is worth.
